note: Do Mi Sol goes from a bare drill over a drone to a tune that skips, then to the chord notes over a backing track. The tune is learned in named stages: with the tune, the tune muted over the chords, then a cappella. The backing track's chords are chord tokens, counted the long way the first time, and the tune and the backing track start slow (40 bpm, moves up to 60); the app writes the line about the slow tempo, and the line about another key is marked {{?key}}, so it shows only with the Key selector. The skip up to Sol carries the one care line, and every high note is on "oo".

exercise.title: Do Mi Sol: skip, sing a tune, sing over chords
exercise.why: Do, Mi and Sol are the three notes of the home chord, so the same skips come back in tune after tune: learn how they sound once and you can sing them in any key.

cells.text:
Press Start exercise below: the drone and the mic start together, and your pitch shows as a line on the staff. Start on a {{1}} that sits easily in your voice and sing {{1}}, {{3}}, {{5}}, then back down. Sing it on the note names.
Then skip straight from {{1}} to {{5}} and back, and hold each note until your line settles on it.
_Don't reach for high notes: start from the low {{1}} when the high one feels tight._
{{?key}}In another key the drone and all three notes sit higher or lower, and each skip is still the same distance.

Press Play below to hear the tune at {{=bpm}}: the mic starts with it. Listen once, then press Play again and sing along. Sing it on "oo".
Sing along with the tune a few times. Then press Tune below to mute the tune, and sing it over the chords alone.
Once that feels easy, press Chords to mute the chords too, and sing the tune a cappella.

Press Start exercise below: the mic and the backing track start together, at {{=bpm}}. The backing track plays {{chord:I}} and {{chord:V}} in turn, one bar each.
{{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of the key, built on {{1}}, and {{chord:V}} is the 5th chord, built on {{5}}. Sing the ringed note over each chord: {{1}} over {{chord:I}}, {{5}} over {{chord:V}}. Sing it on "oo".
Then sing {{3}} over {{chord:I}} in place of {{1}}.
